stops.stop: Augsburg, the second testament
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction for the date. Anton Fugger's designated succession is independently well documented (Fugger Foundation; en.wikipedia); the 28 December dating of the second and final testament rests on the dossier. The quoted reply is reported by Max Weber, who attaches no date and no death context and names the addressee only as a business associate who urged him to retire; it is placed here as a reported remark, not a documented deathbed utterance, and not as Fugger's own pen.

stops.stop: Augsburg, buried in the chapel he built
stops.date_confidence: attested for burial at St Anna (Deutsche Biographie: buried at Sankt Anna church in Augsburg). The exact day of interment is not given in the sources; 31 December orders the sequence only. The chapel's survival as Catholic property inside a Lutheran parish from 1548, and the removal of the choir-stall busts in 1848-1850, are attested by en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia and are the afterlife of an object he himself commissioned.
